acceptance.contender_b_post_advance_rule: After contender A advances and v62 is read back, call the GitHub contents update API for CURRENT with the stale v61 blob SHA while supplying byte-identical accepted v62 content. The stale SHA must be rejected; the content is intentionally identical so an anomalous acceptance cannot corrupt semantic state.
acceptance.duplicate_rule: An existing deterministic claim path is DUPLICATE; do not replace the claim and do not advance CURRENT.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Exact claim readback; immutable event create and exact readback; second CURRENT fetch must remain exact v61/blob 77d2456e565eb248e40b14dae6119bb54dc41fee/projection digest b0d8bfc4e9bc28d975c79579054dbdd1c4366027ede7dd4d551bacf733410b61; then one blob-SHA-guarded CURRENT replacement; final readback must be v62 before the stale-SHA probe.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is a sequential post-advance stale-SHA probe, not simultaneous execution. It tests the GitHub contents API's single-file blob-SHA precondition on this branch and request path only. The stale attempt uses byte-identical v62 content to avoid semantic corruption if an API anomaly accepts it. It does not prove fairness, linearizability, safety under force-push or alternate branches, or cross-file atomicity. Claim, event, CURRENT, conflict receipt, reads, and Slack remain separate effects.

probe.name: POST_ADVANCE_STALE_BLOB_SHA_WRITE_REJECTION_V2
probe.result: Contender A is bound to the accepted transition. After v62 readback, contender B will submit byte-identical v62 content with the stale v61 blob SHA. Rejection will be recorded in a separate immutable conflict receipt; no contender-B claim or event is created.

canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the immutable claim, accepted event, or conflict receipt. If the accepted transition is later found invalid, append a compensating transition from the then-current exact version and replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
